Synopsis:
Iceland held a referendum on whether to reopen EU membership negotiations. 52.8% voted against, 47.2% in favour, with 82.5% voter turnout. Key drivers of the "no" vote were protection of fishing waters (15% of GDP, ~40% of exports), absence of economic urgency, and public satisfaction with existing EEA arrangements. The government had framed EU membership as a geopolitical shield amid Arctic rivalry and Trump-era NATO uncertainty. The result keeps Iceland outside the EU accession process and is a setback for Brussels, which had hoped Iceland's entry could bolster EU enlargement momentum. Iceland remains in the EEA.
